pageText:
Set up Ollama on the shared JupyterHub server. The server runs every notebook in an unprivileged container: there is no root, and sudo is turned off.
In [2]:
import os, platform, shutil
print(platform.platform())
print("user:", os.environ.get("USER"))

Step 1: check which tools are on the PATH already. Only tools inside the home folder can be installed by this user. The image is rebuilt every week from the hub template, so anything installed outside the home folder is gone after the next rebuild, and the next person has to do it all again. Keep every install step in this notebook, so it can be run again from the top after a rebuild.
In [7]:
for tool in ["curl", "tar", "zstd", "ollama"]:
print(f"{tool:8s}", shutil.which(tool))
curl /usr/bin/curl
tar /usr/bin/tar
zstd /usr/bin/zstd
ollama None
In [8]:
!echo $PATH
/opt/conda/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
In [9]:
os.makedirs(os.path.expanduser("~/.local/bin"), exist_ok=True)
os.environ["PATH"] = os.path.expanduser("~/.local/bin") + ":" + os.environ["PATH"]
print(os.environ["PATH"].split(":")[0])
/home/jovyan/.local/bin
In [10]:
!ls -la ~/.local
total 12
drwxr-xr-x 3 jovyan users 4096 Oct 27 09:12 .
drwxr-xr-x 9 jovyan users 4096 Oct 27 09:12 ..
drwxr-xr-x 2 jovyan users 4096 Oct 27 09:12 bin
Step 2: the Ollama release for Linux on x86_64 is one archive, ollama-linux-amd64.tar.zst. It unpacks into bin/ and lib/, so it can live under ~/.local without root. The install script from the website wants root: it writes to /usr/local, creates a system user and a systemd service, and none of that is possible in this container. The archive needs only curl and tar with zstd support, and both are already on the PATH (see the cell above).
In [12]:
!curl -sI https://ollama.com/download/ollama-linux-amd64.tar.zst | head -n 1
HTTP/2 302

Step 3: start the server in the background and pull a small model to check that it works.
In [16]:
import subprocess
server = subprocess.Popen(["ollama", "serve"], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
print(server.pid)
In [17]:
!ollama pull qwen3:0.6b
In [18]:
!ollama list

import requests
r = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate", json={"model": "qwen3:0.6b", "prompt": "Say hi", "stream": False})
print(r.json()["response"])
Step 4: keep the model directory on the persistent disk, so the next session does not pull it again.
In [21]:
